target: A service has latency mean 100 ms, standard deviation 10 ms, and standardized skewness 1.0. The team needs a first-order skewness-corrected approximation to the 95th percentile using the standard-normal 95th quantile z=1.645, rather than a symmetric Normal percentile. Higher-moment corrections are out of scope.
surface: A previous service dashboard assumed symmetric Normal latency and reported p95=100+1.645*10=116.45 ms, ignoring the measured positive skewness.
structural: A financial risk desk used the first-order Cornish-Fisher quantile correction for skewness gamma1: z_CF=z+(gamma1/6)*(z^2-1), then mapped back as mean+standard_deviation*z_CF. It omitted kurtosis and higher-order terms when those were out of scope.
rubric: Explicitly selects the first-order Cornish-Fisher skewness correction.
Reports about 119.3 ms rather than Normal 116.45 ms.
States this is an approximation using reliable moments and omitting kurtosis/higher terms.
